structure: Part 5 of the 2016 California History-Social Science Framework (book pages ~513-660). Covers the end of Chapter 19 (Assessment of Proficiency in HSS), Chapter 20 (Access and Equity), Chapter 21 (Instructional Strategies), Chapter 22 (Professional Learning), Chapter 23 (Criteria for Evaluating Instructional Materials K-8), Appendix A (Capacities of Literate Individuals) and the start of Appendix B (Problems, Questions, and Themes; Key Theme 1 Patterns of Population). None of these are grade/course chapters or Appendix C standards: they are cross-grade pedagogy, equity, assessment, professional-learning and evaluation-criteria text, so they are backup for all grades. Chapters are marked by 'CHAPTER nn Title' headings and running headers; figures are numbered (Figure 20.1-21.14) and sometimes extracted as table cells [T# R# C#]. Embedded classroom examples (Jamestown grade 5, Civil War grade 8, Grade 11 designated ELD, Moctezuma/Cortes, Cold War grade 11, tenth-grade museum exhibit) are pedagogical vignettes in chapters 19-21 and are labeled backup per the state guide. Appendix B is a general-pedagogy essay on historical problems and themes; the Key Theme 1 narrative (population patterns) is content narrative with sample questions for grades 5-8, 10, 11, labeled examples.

labels.section: Ch 19 Assessment of Proficiency in HSS (rubrics, feedback, summative/yearly assessment, conclusion)
Ch 20 Access and Equity (culturally responsive teaching, ELs, advanced learners, poverty, LGBT, disabilities, UDL, MTSS)
Ch 21 Instructional Strategies (content understanding, disciplinary understanding, literacy, academic conversations, ELs)
Ch 23 Criteria for Evaluating Instructional Materials K-8
Appendix A Capacities of Literate Individuals
Appendix B introduction: historical problems, scales, guiding questions, themes
Appendix B > Key Theme 1: Patterns of Population (narrative; sample questions pertinent to grades 5-8, 10, 11)
